segments.oily: Oily-skin reviewers report clearer skin, smaller pores, and improved texture with consistent use, and several say they experienced no breakouts or irritation despite typically reacting to new products.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin are split: some describe worsening dryness, itching, flaking, or burning, while others (using it alongside a moisturizer) report no additional dryness and clearer skin.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers note reduced pore size and improved texture, though one reports a residual layer of oil and leftover dirt after cleansing.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers frequently report stinging or slight burning on first use but say it subsides quickly and does not worsen irritation when paired with moisturizer and sunscreen; a minority report rashes, burning, or dryness severe enough to stop use.
segments.normal: Reviewers describing normal skin report smoother texture and fewer breakouts with twice-daily use and no irritation.
segments.mature: Mature-skin reviewers (40s–70s) report smoother texture, reduced pore size, and fading fine lines, with some noting results appear more slowly than with stronger retinoids.

concerns.aging: Many reviewers say fine lines look plumper or diminished after weeks of use and skin feels smoother; one long-term user with no wrinkles yet used it preventatively, while another after two months saw no visible change in wrinkles or hyperpigmentation.
concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers pairing it with a moisturizer report no added dryness and even hydration or plumper skin, but several describe significant dryness, flakiness, itching, or the need to moisturize every 30 minutes, especially with frequent use.
concerns.redness: Reviewers with redness-prone or sensitive skin report calmer, less red skin over time, though a few describe new rashes or increased sensitivity around the eyes and mouth.
concerns.barrier: Several reviewers state the product helped repair or protect the skin barrier without dryness; one explicitly warns that overusing retinol strength (using more than a pea-sized amount) damages the barrier.
concerns.spots: Numerous reviewers report fading of dark spots, hyperpigmentation, and post-acne marks within weeks to a few months; one three-month user reports no change to dark spots at all.
concerns.blemishes: The large majority describe clearer skin, fewer blackheads/whiteheads and reduced acne scarring, including cases of hormonal, cystic, and body acne improving; a notable minority report no improvement or worsening acne, cystic breakouts, or closed comedones.
concerns.oiliness: Oily-skin reviewers mostly report improved texture and smaller pores without mention of increased oil, though one reviewer with oily/combination skin says a layer of oil remains after cleansing.

aspects.libelle: Stinging or burning on first applications

extraits.texte: As someone who has acne vulgaris and dry, sensitive skin, I found cerave's 4% BPO cleanser to be perfect as its great for comedonal + inflammatory acne without causing dryness as it contains hyaluronic acid in its formula. This makes it perfect for daily usage without dryness or irritability.

I have been using this product off and on for over a year. I have very sensitive skin that is prone to redness and stings when I apply most products. I'm 44 years old and was looking for a retinol that wouldn't irritate my skin. This one really fit well into my skincare regimen. It's not as harsh as others that I've tried, but still makes a visible difference- just probably not as quickly as other stronger products. I would recommend this for anyone with sensitive skin. If you don't have sensitive skin, a product with stronger retinol might show results faster.

I can't stop touching my face, it's so soft and smooth! My boyfriend even noticed the improvement in my skin. I've had texture issues for years and only wish I found this product sooner. My other retinol is going in the trash and this is going to be my new holy grail. I also just got the SA cleanser. Neither of these products have dried out my normal to dry sensitive skin either.

I've had acne prone skin for over a decade. my skincare focus has always been acne based, but now at 31 I've been looking to add more anti-aging products in. I figured a gentle retinol would be great, as it'd help both acne and fine lines. as soon as I started using this, I started breaking out. after taking a deeper look at the ingredients list, I found niacinamide was in it. I can't use products with niacinamide and ALWAYS break out when I find it in skincare I'm using. niacinamide is in just way too much nowadays and after I was getting it in high doses from different products, it started wreaking havoc on my skin and I can no longer use it. if cerava products break you out, check the ingredients. Their products almost ALWAYS contain niacinamide. PLEASE make some niacinamide free products!!!
